PullRequest.Title: Show structural changes in the multi-file diff editor's file list
PullRequest.Body:

Part 3 of 3 stacked PRs that show structural changes in the file list of the multi-file diff editor:

1. #350136: revealing ranges below the first screen in multi-file diffs (merged)
2. #350137: reusable structural diff model, renderer and toggle
3. #350138: structural changes in the multi-file diff editor's file list (this PR)

While the Source Control view shows structural changes (`scm.structuralDiff.enabled`, and Show Structural Diff in its View & Sort menu), the file list of the multi-file diff editor shows them too.

### Change

- Files that a structural diff provider supports can expand to the symbols that changed in them. They start collapsed and load their symbols when they are expanded, with the model of the previous PR. Like in the Source Control view, collapsed files and hidden editors keep no symbols, and a file whose symbols take longer than 800 ms to load shows a loading twistie.
- Opening a symbol reveals it in the diff of its file, with the range reveal of the first PR, and selects it, which also shows it in a hidden unchanged region.
- Symbol rows reuse the renderer, labels and accessible labels of the Source Control view. While structural changes are shown, the accessibility help of the file list tells how to expand files and open symbols.
- In a flat list, all files keep the space of a twistie while files can expand, so that their icons stay aligned. In a tree, files follow the Explorer: those that can expand show a chevron, like file nests.
- File rows show their icon right after their twistie, like folders, and keep their left inset only where the file icon theme hides the twistie. With file icon themes that have folder icons, files therefore move 8px to the left, also while structural changes are off, and line up with folders.
- The Changes editor of the Agents window uses the same file list, so it shows structural changes too. That window has no Source Control view, so Show Structural Diff keeps its default there, which is on.

### Testing

- `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/multiDiffEditor/test/browser/multiDiffEditorWithFileList.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/multiDiffEditor/test/browser/multiDiffEditorConfiguration.test.ts --run src/vs/editor/test/browser/widget/multiDiffEditorWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/test/browser/sessionChangesEditor.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/test/browser/scmStructuralDiff.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/test/browser/scmViewService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/test/common/scmStructuralDiff.test.ts`: passed (153 tests). The new test expands a file, opens a symbol, collapses the file again and turns structural changes on and off.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run valid-layers-check` and `pnpm run check-cyclic-dependencies`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint`, `node --experimental-strip-types build/lib/formatter.ts --verify` and `pnpm run stylelint` on the changed files: passed.
- Component explorer: the new fixtures `editor/multiDiffEditor/withFileList/WithStructuralChanges` (flat list, 4 themes) and `WithStructuralChangesTree` (tree, 2 themes) are stable and render without errors. The screenshots of the 9 existing file list fixtures are identical to those of `main`.
- Two tests in `src/vs/sessions/contrib/chatWindow/test/browser/sessionsChatWindowProvider.test.ts`, about the layout of chat windows, fail on my machine, also on `main`.

To test manually: with `scm.structuralDiff.enabled`, open the changes of a Source Control group that contains TypeScript files, for example with Open Changes, and expand a file in the file list.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The hide path clears StructuralDiffModel.entries without emitting a tree refresh, while both _structuralChanges and the object tree retain the returned elements. Maximizing the panel propagates visibility without clearing editor input, so this is a reachable retention path, not just a hypothetical direct call. Retained byte counts are not measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Structural-diff node payloads, wrapper elements, and object-tree nodes retained by hidden file lists
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained memory grows with the total changed-symbol and coverage payload across expanded files in the hidden editor groups; the retention lasts until the input is cleared, results are replaced, or structural children are explicitly removed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary retained heap and associated GC pressure while the editor area is hidden
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The multi-diff file list contained only files and folders, so hiding the editor retained no structural-diff payloads or structural tree nodes.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Hiding the editor disposes the model entries and their document references, but keeps the computed symbol elements strongly reachable through the file-list map and tree for the hidden editor's lifetime.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The diff adds _structuralChanges, stores computed elements in it at line 486, and installs them in the tree at line 487. The new setVisible(false) path at line 351 only calls the model's setVisible(false); it does not clear either newly added owner of the results.
Findings.Title: Release rendered structural results when hiding the editor
Findings.Impact: After expanding files in a large multi-file diff, maximizing the Terminal/Panel or hiding the editor area for chat keeps the full structural trees alive even though their model cache was released. This can retain substantial symbol/coverage data throughout an extended terminal or chat workflow.
Findings.Evidence: MultiDiffEditorFileList.setVisible calls only _structuralDiff.setVisible before optionally reloading on show. StructuralDiffModel.setVisible(false) calls clear(), which disposes entries but fires no onDidChange event. _structuralChanges.set and _tree.setChildren retain the returned SCMStructuralDiffElement objects, whose node and children fields retain the provider payload. Layout.toggleMaximizedPanel calls setEditorHidden(true), which hides the editor grid view; Part.setVisible -> EditorGroupView.onDidVisibilityChange -> EditorPanes.setVisible forwards visibility without clearInput. Thus ordinary input-clearing on tab switches does not eliminate this panel-maximization case.
Findings.Recommendation: On hiding, clear _structuralChanges and remove structural children from the tree while preserving file expansion/scroll state, then reload expanded files on show as the existing code already does.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a multi-file diff or Agents Changes editor with a flat/tree file list; structural changes disabled or files initially collapsed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing document resolution and initial textual diffs precede the resolved item list. File-list sorting/tree construction is synchronous. Structural computation is not required to open the editor and is not started for initially collapsed files.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve file/remote/virtual document contents for the existing multi-diff documents
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by distinct original/modified document URIs, at most two per two-sided file; shared reference acquisition coalesces identical URIs. Existing view models already hold these documents before structural expansion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The multi-diff editor already resolved and retained its document models before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing cold document loading blocks document availability; warm references avoid new content loading.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N changed files and their distinct document URIs; tree-mode path grouping remains unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing document initialization is unchanged. No structural requests run for collapsed files, and disabled structural mode returns false before resource checks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: StructuralDiffModel is created with the list but holds no entries until expansion. Provider eligibility uses existing models or URI/language matching and performs no file read. WorkerManager creation does not start its worker.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: initial file elements use PreserveOrCollapsed and getChildren is reached through expansion/reload, not list construction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Initial file counts and source-document loading costs vary. No measured startup timings; no evidence of a new heavyweight eager boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup regression: the new structural feature is lazy, and initial source resolution is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand one or several supported files to load changed symbols
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Symbol rows wait for model references, worker text-diff completion, ordered provider evaluation, payload validation/wrapping, and tree insertion. The rest of the file list and ordinary diff navigation remain usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire original and modified text-model references through the URI-keyed resolver
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two acquisitions per cold structural entry, with underlying content resolution shared by canonical URI. Ordinary multi-diff documents are already held, so these normally add references rather than disk/remote reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No structural-entry reference acquisitions occurred in the multi-diff file list; its document models were already held by the existing editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both references must resolve before structural computation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request worker text-diff computation and synchronize models if not already mirrored
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One computeDiff call per uncached structural entry; up to two initial model-sync messages for unsynced URIs, otherwise existing incremental synchronization is reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing diff editors used the worker, but the file list did not issue structural text-diff requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Text-diff completion is required before requesting symbols.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send structural context to extension-host providers and convert returned structural payloads
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Providers are evaluated sequentially until the first successful result. Normally one provider request per uncached file entry; failures/no result may advance to another registered provider. This is not per symbol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Structural providers were available to SCM, but this multi-diff file-list workflow issued no such requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider response and conversion precede symbol-row insertion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the supplied texts and changed ranges to the existing TypeScript server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per TS6 provider invocation; a failed request can open the backing document and retry once. No subprocess is launched per symbol/file by this provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider/server path existed for SCM; expanding files in the multi-diff list did not invoke it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response is required for that file's symbol rows; requests use low priority and the existing server queue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use a shared TypeScript 7 API pipe, isolated snapshots, temporary text updates, and snapshot cleanup
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared coalesced connection on first use, not one pipe per file. Per TS7 invocation: an open snapshot, two sequential temporary updates/source reads, disposal, and a close-files snapshot/disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The shared TS7 provider path existed; the multi-diff file list did not invoke it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations precede completion of the TS7 provider request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: E independently expanded supported files, document text size, changed ranges, and returned symbol/coverage count S. Boundary calls scale with E/provider attempts, not S.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most three active structural load chains per StructuralDiffModel. Each resolves its two references concurrently, then computes text diff and evaluates providers sequentially. Shared worker CPU and the TS6 request queue do not provide three independent CPU lanes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Entries are keyed by DocumentDiffItemViewModel. Pending promises coalesce model/provider work; positive, empty, and failure/status results are cached until invalidation/release. Worker mirrors and resolver references are shared by URI; TS7 connection initialization is shared.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all boundaries were traced from getChildren through the reused model and concrete provider implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency, file sizes, and available provider combinations vary. External native-library internals were not profiled.
Scenarios.Verdict: Expected on-demand feature work, with request coalescing and a three-load limiter; no independent high-confidence regression in the expansion computation path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit an expanded file, change providers/language, or rebuild the list while symbols are displayed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Content invalidation disposes the old entry, then a 150 ms scheduler triggers reload. The old displayed rows remain while the replacement loads; new symbol display requires the same worker/provider chain as expansion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat worker text-diff and structural provider requests for invalidated expanded files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new entry per affected expanded file after coalesced invalidation; repeated callers join entry.pending. Provider changes can invalidate all E expanded files. Not one request per symbol or per keystroke.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This multi-diff file list had no live structural reloads. The same scheduling mechanism already existed in SCM.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only refreshed symbol results wait for these requests; existing displayed rows remain.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build stable symbol identities, wrapper elements, and recursive object-tree elements
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Work scales with returned symbol nodes and their paths. Global rebuilds can reconstruct all displayed structural subtrees, and warm getChildren calls avoid provider work but still apply tree children.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The file list rebuilt file/folder nodes only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Wrapping/tree insertion runs synchronously before refreshed rows appear.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Affected expanded files E, returned symbols S, and invalidation/rebuild frequency after debounce.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Invalidations are coalesced by resource and the 150 ms scheduler; replacement loads use the same per-model three-load limiter. Cancellation can free a load slot before an already-issued external operation finishes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Content changes evict the corresponding entry; provider changes clear entries. Empty/error results do not continuously retry. Previous rows are retained during replacement, while unrelated entries can remain warm.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for debounce, joining, and retained previous rows. No evidence that the diff removes an existing coalescing optimization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large payload and frequent global-rebuild costs are unmeasured. Potential redundant warm tree applications were not promoted without a sufficiently consequential trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence regression. Provider/text work remains bounded by entry caching and debounce; symbol-tree reconstruction is expected feature cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Collapse a file, remove files/change input, disable structural changes, or toggle off the file list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Collapse synchronously removes displayed structural children and releases its model entry. Item replacement releases entries/results absent from the new item set. Turning off the list disposes the list instance.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel structural entries and release their model references; late references are disposed on arrival
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One release per affected cached entry and its acquired references. Multi-diff view models still hold normal document references, so structural release normally does not unload those documents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There were no structural cache entries or structural rows in the file list to clean up.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local tree cleanup is synchronous; late boundary completion/cleanup is not awaited by the UI.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of affected expanded entries and displayed symbol nodes; file removal is checked against a Set of remaining items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entry cancellation settles joined requests and releases limiter slots. List disposal owns listeners/timers; disposableTimeout removes itself from its store on completion/disposal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Collapsed files discard results and reload on expansion. Disabled mode clears model entries and displayed structural rows during rendering. Removed input items are purged from both model entries and _structuralChanges.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: explicit map removal, subtree deletion, releaseWhere, input clearing, and MutableDisposable ownership were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cleanup volume depends on expanded content; no measured disposal timing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression in these explicit cleanup paths. Ordinary tab switches clear editor input and therefore are not the retained-hidden-tree trigger.

Scenarios.Scenario: Maximize the Terminal/Panel or hide the editor area for chat while a multi-diff file list has expanded files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Layout hides the editor grid view and propagates visibility to active panes without clearing input. The new setVisible(false) cancels/releases structural model entries immediately, but does not remove structural results from the list map/tree.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Release structural model entries while the rendered file list remains allocated
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: All E expanded entries are disposed; their S rendered symbol elements and provider payloads remain strongly referenced by _structuralChanges and the object tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hiding the editor retained file/folder list state but no structural-diff payload/tree nodes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No additional external work is required to hide the pane. The regression is retained heap during the subsequent hidden lifetime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload expanded files through the worker/provider chain when the editor area is shown again
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to E uncached structural entries, with model-reference and worker-mirror sharing as in the expansion scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No structural reload occurred on re-show.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Replacement rows wait for asynchronous reload; the rest of the editor can proceed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Sum of changed-symbol and coverage payload across expanded files in hidden editor groups; duration of terminal/chat use controls retention lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hide performs local disposal/cancellation. Re-show uses the existing three-load limiter per model; retained data is independent of request concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The authoritative model cache is cleared on hide, but _structuralChanges and tree nodes keep the old results. Re-show computes replacements rather than reusing those retained results.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: panel maximization -> setEditorHidden -> grid/Part visibility -> EditorGroupView -> EditorPanes.setVisible -> file-list setVisible was traced, including the distinction from clearInput on tab switches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Heap size and prevalence of large expanded symbol sets are not measured; uncertainty affects severity rather than the proven ownership mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity cleanup-lifecycle memory regression: hidden file lists unnecessarily retain structural payloads after their model cache is released.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a structural symbol; toggle the shared structural-diff preference; render SCM rows and accessibility help
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening an already-loaded symbol synchronously reveals its file, obtains the active diff control, sets its selection, and reveals the target range. If textual diff data is not current, range reveal is deferred. Toggle state propagates through one shared observable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist/read the workspace structural-diff choice through the existing storage service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One preference store per toggle and one read per relevant storage-change notification, not per file. Observable equality prevents duplicate state transitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SCMViewPane already persisted and listened for the same workspace key; this PR moves ownership into SCMViewService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: In-memory preference change triggers list/SCM refresh; no collection-sized storage loop is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scroll/rebind virtualized diff UI and obtain position offsets for range reveal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two reveal calls for a symbol open plus one selection update; no structural provider call per symbol click. Range work uses the selected file and existing diff mappings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: File clicks already revealed files. Symbol-specific selection/range reveal is new, using the existing widget path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous UI work for the click, or a cancellable wait for the existing textual diff to become current.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User symbol opens, visible virtualized rows, selected-file diff mappings, and files refreshed by preference changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Symbol reveal is synchronous, with one replaceable pending range-reveal operation if a textual diff is pending. Toggle propagation is observable-driven; renderer templates remain virtualized and dispose hover/listener ownership.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Symbol opens require a current cached structural generation. No new symbol computation is requested by opening a row. Shared preferences retain existing workspace semantics.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the traced call flow; renderer/style changes and generic adapter extraction preserve existing SCM computation cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No profiling of scroll/rebinding cost. No concrete evidence of forced-layout amplification sufficient for a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent regression: shared SCM changes mostly relocate existing state/renderer behavior, and new symbol navigation reuses bounded existing reveal mechanisms.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass across all 20 changed files and every diff page. Traced lazy expansion, live invalidation, cache/concurrency behavior, cleanup, actual hidden-editor visibility, navigation, shared preferences, worker/extension-host/server boundaries, and payload ownership. Submitted one high-confidence introduced memory-retention finding. No concrete old performance regression fix was established for blame/fix-learning reporting. Static review; external provider/library duration and retained bytes were not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
